e.g. Q2FVT1 Lysostaphin resistance protein A LyrA Staphylococcus aureus
* **Description of issue**
from UniProt user request 274344 (Paul Denny)
Hi curators !
I think that both the ARBA- derived GO annotations may be inappropriately applied. LyrA is probably not an endopeptidase . Also probably doesn’t undergo CAAX-box protein maturation, despite having CAAX box motif, because bacteria don’t seem to have c-terminal prenylation of proteins. So perhaps these ARBA need taxon constraints added?
...

Just discovered I was wrong, bacterial proteins are prenylated eg see:
advs7092-gra-0001-m.jpg
[Structure Prediction and Genome Mining‐Aided Discovery of the Bacterial C‐Terminal Tryptophan Prenyltransferase PalQ](https://advanced.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/advs.202307372)
[onlinelibrary.wiley.com](https://advanced.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/advs.202307372)
However , it seems that the enzymatic mechanism is different to eukaryotes.
Elisabeth:
 "eukaryotic" is mentioned in the definition of https://www.ebi.ac.uk/QuickGO/term/GO:0080120 :

"A series of specific posttranslational modifications to the CAAX box region of CAAX box proteins. CAAX box proteins are eukaryotic proteins that contain..."

It might be more consistent to have ARBA ARBA00026983 restrict the InterPro signature IPR003675 to "eukaryota" as it is already done for FunFam. Or could such a constraint be added to GO?
